CAPABILITIES & LIMITS

Clear limits.
Better decisions.

A decision-support prototype for fixed-fee projects, with bounded autonomy and explicit assumptions.

What works today

  • Budget, working-day deadline, and resource-return disruptions.
  • Dependency-aware scheduling with one task per resource.
  • Approved alternatives and optional-scope deferral.
  • Hard budget, deadline, required scope, and margin constraints.
  • Multi-objective ranking and a Pareto frontier within explored candidates.
  • Review, verification, approval, stale-plan checks, undo, and JSON export.
  • Editable validated plans; storage in this browser only.

What to confirm yourself

  • Backup capacity and quoted prices are declared assumptions.
  • Optional scope deferral needs agreement with the client.
  • Durations and costs are estimates; there is no uncertainty distribution.
  • “Verified” means declared constraints pass, not real-world facts are independently confirmed.
  • Margin and lateness costs are scenario calculations, not accounting forecasts.

Operational boundaries

  • 24 tasks, 12 resources, 3 alternatives per task.
  • 512 candidate assignments per run; truncation is disclosed.
  • 8 workflow events, 2,000 input characters.
  • Live interpretation: one API call, 15-second timeout, 700 output tokens.
  • Local API: 64 KB payloads, 10 calls per minute per IP.
  • Whole INR rupees; at most 365 working days.

Not production claims

  • The schedule is a deterministic heuristic, not a global optimum.
  • No work calendar, holidays, partial progress, or task preemption.
  • No Jira, billing, email, or vendor-booking integration.
  • No authentication, team collaboration, or encrypted browser storage.
  • Hosted demo uses local rules; live OpenAI needs the local server and a server-side key.
  • AI output can be semantically wrong even when schema-valid; review the interpretation.
  • No fabricated human feedback or claimed customer savings.
